userPrompt: Can a company in the EU refuse to give an employee their statutory annual leave?
responseText:
**No, a company in the EU cannot lawfully refuse an employee their statutory annual leave.**

### Key rules under EU law
- **Directive 2003/88/EC** (Working Time Directive) gives every worker a **minimum of 4 weeks (20 working days)** of paid annual leave per year. This right is mandatory and cannot be waived by contract, collective agreement, or employer decision.
- The entitlement accrues from the first day of employment and is protected even during probation.
- Employers must allow employees to **actually take** this leave. It is not enough to merely “offer” it or pay it out while the employee continues working.

### What an employer cannot do
- Refuse a properly requested leave period without an objectively justified business reason (and even then they must offer an alternative period).
- Force an employee to forfeit unused leave at the end of the leave year (except in very limited cases when the employee was genuinely unable to take it).
- Replace statutory leave with sick leave, garden leave, or other forms of absence.
- Pay the employee in lieu of leave, except upon termination of the employment contract.

### Limited exceptions
- Employers may **postpone** leave in genuine cases of business necessity (e.g. key staff shortages during a peak period), but they must allow the employee to take the leave within **18 months** following the end of the leave year in which it was earned.
- Some Member States grant more than 20 days (e.g. 25–30 days). National law then applies to the extra days.

### Practical outcome
If an employer simply refuses to grant statutory annual leave, the employee can:
1. File a formal complaint with the national labour inspectorate.
2. Bring a claim before the labour court (most EU countries treat this as an automatic unfair detriment; some treat it as a breach of contract or discrimination).
3. Claim compensation, payment for untaken leave, and/or damages.

**Bottom line:** Statutory annual leave is a non-negotiable EU social right. A company cannot lawfully refuse it. Any attempt to do so exposes the employer to claims, fines, and reputational damage.
